what: Three signal-domain and paper passes in the C++ core (ADR 0019): crt-classic (the Studio's tube stage, web/shaders/crt-classic with its CPU reference web/shaders/reference/retro-crt.mjs), VHS (web/shaders/vhs) and fibre-network watercolour (web/shaders/fibre). Same links as the earlier bounds files: JavaScript reference against the C++ reference (CPU link), and the C++ reference against the one WGSL source on D3D12 (WARP), WebGPU (SwiftShader) and Vulkan (lavapipe). Written before the C++ references, the WGSL rewrites and the first run of any of the three.
controls: Every link carries a built-in control that must fail on every case of every run; a run whose control passes fails as a whole. Separately, one constant in the C++ reference and one in style.wgsl are edited by hand for each pass, rebuilt and run, the result recorded in evidence/cpp-port-style-runs-5.json with the prediction below, and the edit reverted.

crt_classic.fixtures: The seven cases of evidence/shaders-crt-classic-parity-bounds.json, frames built as web/test/shaders-classic.html builds them: testCard(240, 150) nearest-upscaled x4 (960 x 600), testCard(320, 200) x3 (960 x 600), gradientPlate(960, 600). The JavaScript reference is crtStage of retro-crt.mjs (classicRef), RGBA8 in and out. Its transfer tables (TO_LIN as f32, TO_SRGB as u8), and for each case the 8.8 fixed beam and mask tables, are exported too.
crt_classic.reference_arithmetic: The JavaScript reference is integer and Float32Array arithmetic (8.8 fixed point, f32 tables, f32 glow buffers with float64 running sums). The C++ reference keeps each f32 store and each integer truncation where the JavaScript has one.

cpu_link.tables_equal: the C++ TO_LIN, TO_SRGB, beam and mask tables equal the exported ones, every entry
cpu_link.why: Integer and f32-store arithmetic with the transcendental functions only in the tables, which are compared entry by entry; a faithful port reproduces every byte.

gpu_link.why: The web bound (M1 criterion 9: within 1/255 at 8 bits). The GPU blurs with direct sums where the reference keeps a running sum, so a glow value can round differently.

controls.built_in: The C++ reference with every option of the case that is above zero among scanStrength, beam, maskStrength, bloom, halation, curvature, aberration and vignette multiplied by 1.1: at least one byte differs on the CPU link, and the GPU's maximum difference from it exceeds 1 code, on every case.
controls.source_edit: C++: the bloom weight 0.9 to 0.95 in the glow field. Prediction: the CPU link fails on studio-defaults and glow-strong (the cases with bloom) and on no other case. WGSL: the halation weight 0.3 to 0.33 in the glow add pass. Prediction: WARP fails on glow-strong and on no case without halation (slot-strong, dot-cell3, tube-strong, flat-cell1, vignette-only).

vhs.fixtures: The three cases of evidence/shaders-vhs-parity-bounds.json, source built as web/test/shaders-vhs.html builds it: streetScene(176, 120, 0), each value 1 - exp(-2.4 v) sRGB-encoded, alpha 1. The JavaScript createVhs frame (sample, tape, playback) gives the signal (Float32Array, lines x N x 4) and toDisplay gives the 352 x 240 RGBA8 display; both are exported, with the plan (N, the three tap sets, delay, the generation-scaled noise and phase values, the YIQ inverse).
vhs.reference_arithmetic: The JavaScript stores each pass's output in a Float32Array and computes in float64 between. The C++ reference keeps those f32 stores.

cpu_link.plan_equal: N and the tap counts equal; every tap, the delay, the noise and phase scales and the YIQ inverse within 1e-12 relative
cpu_link.display_mismatch: codes equal except where the JavaScript signal value lies within 255e-5 codes of a rounding edge (x.5); at most 1e-4 of the display's channel values a case
cpu_link.why: The noise draws use log, cos and sin, whose last bit may differ between V8 and the C++ library; each pass rounds to f32, so a last-bit difference stays near one f32 rounding.

gpu_link.why: The web bounds: the same integer hashes on both sides; f32 against float64 in the filters, the Box-Muller transform and the line shifts, and a dropout run boundary moving a sample on a half step.

controls.built_in: The C++ reference with the luma noise multiplied by 1.5: it must exceed signal_max_abs on the CPU link and the GPU bounds, on every case.
controls.source_edit: C++: the chroma-noise knot spacing 24 to 25 samples. Prediction: the CPU link fails on every case. WGSL: the dropout segment length 64 to 63 in the playback pass. Prediction: WARP fails on ep-rental-tracking (the most dropouts); the other cases may pass.

fibre.fixtures: The three cases of evidence/shaders-fibre-parity-bounds.json at 320 x 200: displayLinear('street') with cold-press and hot-press, displayLinear('edges') with rough. The exporter takes the suspended and deposited pigment (float64, runFibre keep) and forms the float64 output paper exp(-(P + D)), checking that Math.fround of each value equals runFibre's own frame.

cpu_link.rule: |cpp - js| <= 1e-9 max(1, |js|) on every output value; displayEncode8 codes equal except at a rounding edge within 1e-9 (at most 2 a case)

gpu_link.why: The web bounds: explicit diffusion steps on both sides, contractive; the fibre network is rasterised from integer hashes identically.

controls.built_in: The C++ reference with the wash strength multiplied by 1.1: it must exceed value_max_rel on the CPU link and the GPU bound, on every case.
controls.source_edit: C++: the tensor smoothing radius 3 to 2. Prediction: the CPU link fails on every case. WGSL: the initial wetness floor 0.05 to 0.2 in the init pass. Prediction: WARP fails on at least edges-rough.
